metadata.title: A new proof of Gromov's theorem on groups of polynomial growth

nodes.name: Polynomial growth and weakly polynomial growth
nodes.statement: $G$ has $\textbf{polynomial growth}$ if for some $d\in(0,\infty)$, $\limsup_{r\to\infty} |B_G(r)|/r^d < \infty$; $G$ has $\textbf{weakly polynomial growth}$ if for some $d$, $\liminf_{r\to\infty} |B_G(r)|/r^d < \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: A finitely generated group has polynomial (resp. weakly polynomial) growth if its word-ball cardinality is bounded above (resp. has a bounded subsequence) by a polynomial in the radius.

nodes.name: Degree of growth
nodes.statement: The $\textbf{degree of growth}$ of $G$ is $\deg(G) = \min\{d \in \mathbb{N}_{\ge 0} : \liminf_{r\to\infty} V(r)/r^d < \infty\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The degree of growth of a group is the smallest nonnegative integer d for which the liminf of V(r)/r^d is finite.

nodes.name: Energy function of a group action
nodes.statement: Given an action $G \acts X$ on a metric space $X$, the $\textbf{energy function}$ $E:X\to\mathbb{R}$ is $E(x)=\sum_{s\in S} d^2(sx,x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The energy of a point under a group action is the sum of squared displacements over the generating set.

nodes.name: Property (T)
nodes.statement: $G$ has $\textbf{Property (T)}$ iff every isometric action of $G$ on a Hilbert space has a fixed point.
nodes.statement_clean: Kazhdan's Property (T): every isometric Hilbert-space action of G has a fixed point.

nodes.name: Harmonic map on a graph
nodes.statement: $f:\Gamma\to\h$ is $\textbf{harmonic}$ iff its restriction to each edge has constant derivative and for every vertex $v$, $\sum_{d(w,v)=1}(f(w)-f(v))=0$.
nodes.statement_clean: A piecewise smooth map from a graph to a Hilbert space is harmonic iff it is affine on edges and satisfies the discrete mean-value property at vertices.

nodes.name: Finite dimensionality of polynomial-growth harmonic functions (Colding-Minicozzi)
nodes.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a Cayley graph of a group $G$ of weakly polynomial growth and $d\in[0,\infty)$. Then the space of harmonic functions on $\Gamma$ with polynomial growth at most $d$ is finite dimensional.
assumptions: $G$ is a finitely generated group of weakly polynomial growth
conclusions: The space of harmonic functions on $\Gamma$ with polynomial growth at most $d$ is finite dimensional.

nodes.name: Poincare inequality for finitely generated groups
nodes.statement: For every $R\in[0,\infty)\cap\mathbb{Z}$ and every smooth $f:B(3R)\to\mathbb{R}$, $\int_{B(R)}|f-f_R|^2 \le 8|S|^2 R^2 \frac{V(2R)}{V(R)} \int_{B(3R)} |\nabla f|^2$.
assumptions: $G$ a finitely generated group with finite generating set $S$

nodes.name: Technical finite dimensionality bound (Theorem 3.1')
nodes.statement: For every $d\in(0,\infty)$ there is $C=C(d)\in(0,\infty)$ such that if $\liminf_{R\to\infty} V(R)(\det Q_R)^{1/\dim\V}/R^d < \infty$, then $\dim\V < C$.
assumptions: $\V$ is a $2k$-dimensional vector space of harmonic functions on $\Gamma$

nodes.name: Equivalent characterizations of Property (T)
nodes.statement: The following are equivalent for $G$: (1) $G$ has Property (T); (2) $\exists D$ such that for any isometric $G\acts\h$, $G$ fixes a point in $B(x,D\sqrt{E(x)})$; (3) $\exists D,\lambda\in(0,1)$ giving $x'\in B(x,D\sqrt{E(x)})$ with $E(x')\le\lambda E(x)$; (4) no isometric action $G\acts\h$ has $E$ attaining a positive minimum.
assumptions: $G$ a finitely generated group with symmetric generating set $S$
nodes.origin_citation: weak version of Fisher-Margulis; Ghys-de la Harpe random groups

nodes.name: Selection of good scales $i_1, i_2$
nodes.statement: There are integers $i_1,i_2\in[i_0,\infty)$ with $i_2-i_1\in(w,3w)$, $h(i_2+1)-h(i_1)<wa$, and $h(i_1+1)-h(i_1)<a$, $h(i_2+1)-h(i_2)<a$.
conclusions: Existence of $i_1, i_2$ with the three properties listed.

nodes.name: Properties of the controlled cover $\B$
nodes.statement: (1) Covers $\B$ and $3\B$ have multiplicity $<e^a$; (2) $|J|<e^{wa}$; (3) for every $j$ and smooth $v:3B_i\to\mathbb{R}$, $\int_{B_i}|v-v_{B_i}|^2 \le C e^a R_1^2 \int_{3B_i} |\nabla v|^2$.
conclusions: Bounded multiplicity, bounded cardinality, and a local Poincare inequality on the cover balls.

nodes.name: Harmonic and non-harmonic bound via $\Phi$
nodes.statement: $\exists C$ depending only on $|S|$: (1) for smooth $u$ on $B(16R_2)$, $Q_{R_2}(u,u) \le C V(R_1)|\Phi(u)|^2 + Ce^{2a}R_1^2\int_{B(2R_2)}|\nabla u|^2$; (2) for harmonic $u$, $Q_{R_2}(u,u) \le C V(R_1)|\Phi(u)|^2 + Ce^{2a}(R_1/R_2)^2 Q_{16R_2}(u,u)$.
conclusions: Two-term estimates of $Q_{R_2}(u,u)$ in terms of $|\Phi(u)|^2$ and either gradient norm or $Q_{16R_2}$.

nodes.name: Selecting controlled-growth subspace $\U$
nodes.statement: There is a subspace $\U\subset\V$ of dimension $\ge k=\dim\V/2$ such that for every $u\in\U$, $Q_{16R_2}(u,u) \le e^{2a} Q_{R_2}(u,u)$.
assumptions: $\V$ a $2k$-dimensional vector space of harmonic functions
conclusions: A half-dimensional subspace $\U$ on which the doubling-type bound $Q_{16R_2}\le e^{2a}Q_{R_2}$ holds.

nodes.name: Harmonic map exists iff no Property (T)
nodes.statement: The following are equivalent: (1) $G$ does not have Property (T); (2) there is an isometric action $G\acts\h$ on a Hilbert space and a nonconstant $G$-equivariant harmonic map $f:\Gamma\to\h$.
assumptions: $G$ a finitely generated group with symmetric generating set $S$

nodes.name: Infinite linear representation of weakly polynomial growth groups
nodes.statement: If $G$ is an infinite group of weakly polynomial growth, then $G$ admits a finite dimensional linear representation $G\to GL(n,\mathbb{R})$ with infinite image.
assumptions: $G$ is an infinite finitely generated group of weakly polynomial growth
conclusions: $G$ admits a finite dimensional linear representation with infinite image.

nodes.name: Gromov's theorem (virtual nilpotence)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a group with weakly polynomial growth, then $G$ is virtually nilpotent.
assumptions: $G$ is a finitely generated group with weakly polynomial growth
conclusions: $G$ has a finite-index nilpotent subgroup (i.e., is virtually nilpotent).

nodes.name: Reverse Poincare inequality for harmonic functions
nodes.statement: For harmonic $v$ on $B(16R_2)$: $R_2^2 \int_{B(2R_2)} |\nabla v|^2 \le C\, Q_{16R_2}(v,v)$.

nodes.name: Energy critical-point characterization
nodes.statement: $x\in\h$ is a critical point of $E$ iff $x$ minimizes $E$ iff $\sum_{s\in S}(x-sx)=0$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Poincare inequality (Theorem thmpi)
nodes.statement: Bound $\int_{B(R)}|f-f_R|^2$ by $\frac{1}{V(R)}\int_{B(R)\times B(R)}|f(p_1)-f(p_2)|^2$, expand into edge-pair sums, apply Cauchy-Schwarz along shortest paths, and use a multiplicity bound on the path map to conclude.

nodes.name: Define edge-energy density $\delta f$ and shortest paths
nodes.statement: Set $\delta f(x)=\int_{B(x,1)}|\nabla f|^2$ and choose a shortest vertex path $\gamma_y$ from $e$ to each $y\in G$.

nodes.name: Multiplicity bound on the path map
nodes.statement: For $y\in B_G(2R-2)$, $\sum_{x\in B(R-1)}\sum_{i=0}^{|y|}(\delta f)(x\gamma_y(i)) \le 2R \sum_{z\in B(3R-1)} (\delta f)(z)$, since the map $(x,i)\mapsto x\gamma_y(i)$ is at most $2R$-to-$1$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz on edge pairs
nodes.statement: For ordered edge pairs $(e_1,e_2)\subset B(R)$ with $d(x_1,x_2)\le 2R-2$ and $y=x_1^{-1}x_2$: $\int_{e_1\times e_2} |f(p_1)-f(p_2)|^2 \le 2R \sum_{i=0}^{|y|}(\delta f)(x_1\gamma_y(i))$.

nodes.name: Sum over edge pairs and combine
nodes.statement: Bound $\int_{B(R)}|f-f_R|^2 \le \frac{1}{V(R)}\int_{B(R)^2}|f(p_1)-f(p_2)|^2$, decompose into edge-pair integrals, apply step 3, then use the at-most-$|S|^2$-to-one map $(e_1,e_2)\mapsto(x_1,y)$ and step 2 to obtain the claimed bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma on good scales
nodes.statement: Find $j_0$ with $h(i_0+3w(j_0+1))-h(i_0+3wj_0)<wa$ (else contradicts the liminf bound), then locate $i_1, i_2$ inside $[m,m+w)$ and $[m+2w,m+3w)$ on which $h$ has small one-step jumps.

nodes.name: Find $j_0$ with $wa$-controlled block
nodes.statement: Argue by contradiction: if no such $j_0$ existed, telescoping would give $h(i_0+3wl)\ge h(i_0)+wal$, violating $\liminf(h(i)-di\log 16)<\infty$.

nodes.name: Locate $i_1,i_2$ inside the block
nodes.statement: Set $m=i_0+3wj_0$; if no $i_1\in[m,m+w)$ and $i_2\in[m+2w,m+3w)$ with single-step jumps $<a$ existed, $h(m+w)-h(m)\ge wa$ or $h(m+3w)-h(m+2w)\ge wa$, contradicting the choice of $j_0$.

nodes.name: Verify $h(i_2+1)-h(i_1)<wa$
nodes.statement: Conclude $h(i_2+1)-h(i_1)\le h(m+3w)-h(m)<wa$, completing the lemma.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma lembmisc
nodes.statement: Bound multiplicity by comparing $V(3R_1)/V(R_1/2)$ to $e^a$ via $h(i_1+1)-h(i_1)<a$; bound $|J|$ via the disjointness of half-balls and $V(2R_2)/V(R_1/2)<e^{wa}$; bound the local Poincare term using Theorem thmpi and translation invariance.

nodes.name: Multiplicity bound for $3\B$
nodes.statement: If $z\in 3B_{j_1}\cap\ldots\cap 3B_{j_l}$, the half-balls $B(x_{j_m},R_1/2)$ are disjoint subsets of $B(x_{j_1},8R_1)$, hence $\log l \le \log V(3R_1)-\log V(R_1/2)\le h(i_1+1)-h(i_1)<a$.

nodes.name: Cardinality bound for $|J|$
nodes.statement: Disjoint half-balls $B(x_j,R_1/2)$ lie in $B(2R_2)$, so $|J|\le V(2R_2)/V(R_1/2) \le V(16^{i_2+1})/V(16^{i_1}) < e^{wa}$.

nodes.name: Local Poincare on $B_i$
nodes.statement: By Theorem thmpi and translation invariance, $\int_{B_i}|v-v_{B_i}|^2 \le 8|S|^2 R_1^2 (V(2R_1)/V(R_1)) \int_{3B_i}|\nabla v|^2 \le 8|S|^2 R_1^2 e^a \int_{3B_i}|\nabla v|^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of harmonic-bound lemma
nodes.statement: Decompose $Q_{R_2}(u,u)$ via the cover $\B$ into $|\Phi_j(u)|^2$ and $|u-\Phi_j(u)|^2$ pieces, bound each using cover cardinality and local Poincare, then for the harmonic case substitute the Schoen-Yau reverse Poincare.

nodes.name: Three-term decomposition over the cover
nodes.statement: Bound $Q_{R_2}(u,u)\le \sum_{j} \int_{B_j} u^2 \le 2\sum_j \int_{B_j} (|\Phi_j(u)|^2 + |u-\Phi_j(u)|^2)$.

nodes.name: Bound the projection term
nodes.statement: $\sum_j \int_{B_j} |\Phi_j(u)|^2 = \sum_j |B_j||\Phi_j(u)|^2 \le C V(R_1)|\Phi(u)|^2$.

nodes.name: Bound the oscillation term
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma lembmisc(3) to each $B_i$: $\sum_j \int_{B_j} |u-\Phi_j(u)|^2 \le Ce^a R_1^2 \sum_j \int_{3B_j}|\nabla u|^2 \le Ce^{2a} R_1^2 \int_{B(2R_2)}|\nabla u|^2$ (using bounded multiplicity).

nodes.name: Apply reverse Poincare for harmonic case
nodes.statement: For harmonic $u$ on $B(16R_2)$, substitute $R_2^2 \int_{B(2R_2)}|\nabla u|^2 \le C Q_{16R_2}(u,u)$ (Schoen-Yau) into the non-harmonic bound to obtain inequality (3.10).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma lemselectu
nodes.statement: Pick a $Q_{R_2}$-orthonormal, $Q_{16R_2}$-orthogonal basis. Show that the count of basis vectors with $Q_{16R_2}\ge e^{2a}$ is $<k$; otherwise $\log(\det Q_{16R_2}/\det Q_R)^{1/2k}\ge (l/k)a$ contradicts $h(i_2+1)-h(i_2)<a$.

nodes.name: Choose simultaneous diagonalizing basis
nodes.statement: Since $Q_{R_2}$ is positive definite, choose a $Q_{R_2}$-orthonormal basis $\beta=\{v_1,\ldots,v_{2k}\}$ that is $Q_{16R_2}$-orthogonal.

nodes.name: Determinant ratio contradiction
nodes.statement: If $\ge l$ vectors have $Q_{16R_2}(v,v)\ge e^{2a}$, then $\log(\det Q_{16R_2}/\det Q_{R_2})^{1/2k}\ge (l/k)a$. But $a > h(i_2+1)-h(i_2) \ge \log\det Q_{16R_2}^{1/2k} - \log\det Q_{R_2}^{1/2k}$. Contradiction if $l\ge k$.

nodes.name: Form $\U$ from controlled basis vectors
nodes.statement: Choose a $k$-element subset $\{u_1,\ldots,u_k\}\subset\beta$ with $Q_{16R_2}(u_j,u_j)<e^{2a}$. Then every element of $\U=\span\{u_1,\ldots,u_k\}$ satisfies $Q_{16R_2}\le e^{2a} Q_{R_2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem thmfinitedim' (dimension bound)
nodes.statement: Choose $w$ minimal with $(R_1/R_2)^2 < 1/(2Ce^{4a})$. Show $\Phi|_\U$ is injective by combining the harmonic bound with Lemma lemselectu, hence $\dim\V = 2\dim\U \le 2|J| \le 2e^{wa}$ which is bounded by a constant depending only on $d$.

nodes.name: Choose smallest $w$ with $(R_1/R_2)^2$ tiny
nodes.statement: Let $w$ be the smallest integer such that $(R_1/R_2)^2 = 2\cdot 16^{i_1-i_2} < 2\cdot 16^{-w} < 1/(2Ce^{4a})$, hence $e^{wa}\le 64 C e^{64 d^2 \log 16}$.

nodes.name: Show $\Phi|_\U$ is injective
nodes.statement: If $u\in\U$ lies in $\ker\Phi$, the harmonic bound gives $Q_{R_2}(u,u)\le Ce^{2a}(R_1/R_2)^2 Q_{16R_2}(u,u) \le Ce^{2a}(R_1/R_2)^2 e^{2a} Q_{R_2}(u,u) \le \frac12 Q_{R_2}(u,u)$, forcing $u=0$.

nodes.name: Conclude dimension bound
nodes.statement: $\dim\V = 2\dim\U \le 2|J| \le 2e^{wa} \le 128\, C\, e^{64 d^2 \log 16}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary corinfiniterep
nodes.statement: Show $G$ is amenable hence lacks Property (T). Use Mok / Korevaar-Schoen to obtain a fixed-point-free isometric $G$-action on a Hilbert space $\h$ and a nonconstant $G$-equivariant harmonic map $f$. Pull back via $\h^*$ to harmonic functions; finite dimensionality (Theorem thmfinitedim) confines the image of $f$ to a finite dimensional $G$-invariant affine subspace, giving the desired representation.

nodes.name: Show $G$ is amenable
nodes.statement: If $V(R_k)<AR_k^d$, find $r_k\in[R_k/2,R_k]$ with $|\partial B_G(r_k)|<3AR_k^{d-1}$, so $\{B_G(r_k)\}$ is a Folner sequence for $G$.

nodes.name: Obtain $G$-equivariant harmonic map
nodes.statement: Amenability implies no Property (T); by Mok / Korevaar-Schoen there is a fixed-point-free isometric action $G\acts\h$ and a nonconstant $G$-equivariant harmonic map $f:\Gamma\to\h$.

nodes.name: Construct linear map $\Phi:\h^*\to\V$
nodes.statement: Each $\phi\in\h^*$ gives a Lipschitz harmonic function $\phi\circ f$. By Theorem thmfinitedim, $\V$ is finite dimensional, so $\ker(\Phi)$ has finite codimension and $\ker(\Phi)^\perp\subset\h$ is finite dimensional and contains $\im f$.

nodes.name: Build finite-dimensional representation
nodes.statement: The affine hull $A$ of $\im f$ is finite dimensional and $G$-invariant. $G\acts A$ cannot factor through a finite group (would have fixed points). Hence $G\to\isom(A)$ is the desired finite dimensional representation with infinite image.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary corgromov by induction on degree
nodes.statement: Induct on $\deg(G)$. Base: degree 0 means finite. Inductive step: by Corollary corinfiniterep get an infinite linear image $H\subset GL(n)$. Apply Tits/Shalom and Wolf-Milnor to get $H$ virtually nilpotent. Then get a short exact sequence $1\to K\to G\to\Z\to 1$, apply Wilkie's lemma to bound $\deg(K)$, and conclude by the inductive hypothesis.

nodes.name: Base case: degree 0
nodes.statement: A group whose degree of growth is 0 is finite, hence virtually nilpotent.

nodes.name: Get infinite linear image $H$
nodes.statement: Assume inductively all groups of degree $\le d-1$ are virtually nilpotent and $\deg(G)=d$. Then $G$ is infinite and Corollary corinfiniterep yields a representation $G\to GL(n)$ with infinite image $H$.

nodes.name: Apply Tits/Wolf-Milnor to make $H$ nilpotent
nodes.statement: Since $H$ has polynomial growth, by Tits' alternative (or Shalom) $H$ is virtually solvable, and by Wolf-Milnor virtually nilpotent.

nodes.name: Construct short exact sequence and bound $\deg(K)$
nodes.statement: After passing to finite-index subgroups assume $H$ nilpotent with torsion-free abelianization, giving $1\to K\to G\to\Z\to 1$. By Wilkie Lemma (2.1), $K$ is finitely generated and $\deg(K)\le\deg(G)-1$.

nodes.name: Combine $K$ nilpotent with cyclic lift to finish
nodes.statement: By the inductive hypothesis $K$ is virtually nilpotent. Take $K'\trianglelefteq G$ a normal finite-index nilpotent subgroup of $K$ and $L\subset G$ infinite cyclic mapping isomorphically to $\Z$. Then $K'L\subset G$ is finite-index solvable; by Wolf-Milnor it is virtually nilpotent.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem thma1 (Property (T) equivalences)
nodes.statement: Show (2)$\implies$(1) trivially; (1)$\implies$(4) since $E$ vanishes at fixed points; (3)$\implies$(2) by iterating to a Cauchy sequence whose limit is a fixed point; (4)$\implies$(3) by contradiction via rescaling and ultralimits.

nodes.name: Easy implications (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) and (1)$\Rightarrow$(4)
nodes.statement: (2) implies (1) immediately. (1) implies (4) since the energy function vanishes at any fixed point.

nodes.name: Iterate to fixed point: (3)$\Rightarrow$(2)
nodes.statement: Define $x_{k+1}\in B(x_k,D\sqrt{E(x_k)})$ with $E(x_{k+1})\le\lambda E(x_k)$. Then $\{x_k\}$ is Cauchy with limit $x_\infty$ satisfying $E(x_\infty)=0$ and $d(x_\infty,x_0)\le D\sqrt{E(x_0)}/(1-\sqrt\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Ultralimit construction: (4)$\Rightarrow$(3) contrapositive
nodes.statement: Assume (3) fails: for each $k$ find $G\acts\h_k$ and $x_k\in\h_k$ with $E(y) > (1-1/k)E(x_k)$ for all $y\in B(x_k,k\sqrt{E(x_k)})$. Rescale $\h_k$ by $1/\sqrt{E(x_k)}$ to get $E(x_k)=1$ and $E(y)\ge 1-1/k$ on $B(x_k,k)$. Take an ultralimit; the resulting action on $\h_\omega$ has $E(x_\omega)=1=\inf E$, so (4) fails.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma harmonic-map iff no Property (T)
nodes.statement: (1)$\Rightarrow$(2): use Theorem thma1 to get an action with $E(x)=\inf E>0$, define $f(g)=gx$ extended affinely on edges; then $f$ is harmonic and nonconstant. (2)$\Rightarrow$(1): if a nonconstant equivariant harmonic map exists, $f(e)$ is a positive minimum of $E$, so $G$ has no fixed point hence lacks Property (T).

nodes.name: Cayley graph viewed as 1-dim simplicial complex
nodes.statement: $\Gamma$ is treated as the geometric realization of a 1-dimensional simplicial complex (not as a discrete space); thus $B_G(R)$ is finite while $B(R)$ is typically 1-dimensional.

nodes.name: Wilkie-Van Den Dries refinement applications
nodes.statement: Several applications of the Wilkie-Van Den Dries refinement of Gromov's theorem (e.g. Varopoulos' isoperimetric theorem) do not follow from the original statement but do follow from the weakly polynomial growth version proved here.

nodes.name: Saloff-Coste credit for Theorem thmpi
nodes.statement: Although Theorem thmpi is not in the literature, the proof is virtually contained in Coulhon-Saloff-Coste pp. 308-310; Saloff-Coste suggested this clean form to replace the author's earlier, more complicated Poincare inequality.
